provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The generator builds nested L-shaped layers around the top-left corner. Layer k is the set of cells with max(r, c) = k, and it is coloured colors[k]. Cells beyond the colour list are background 0. The output is 2n x 2n, and layer k is coloured colors[k % len].

Under D4 the anchor corner moves. Reversing each row (d4 >= 4) sends top-left to top-right. Each clockwise rotation then moves the corner one step: TL -> TR -> BR -> BL. The factory picks the visible anchor corner from d4 and bakes it in as TOP/LEFT constants.

The emitted program measures layer distance from that corner as max(dr, dc). It reads layer colours along the diagonal from the corner. It drops background layers (palette[0]), matching the archived solver's removal of zeros. It then paints the doubled canvas with seq[dist % period].
draft_notes.limitations: Like the archived solver, any layer whose colour equals palette[0] is dropped from the period. This only matters if the generator could produce colour 0 inside the colour list, which random_color presumably avoids. The program assumes square inputs, as the constructor always produces them. Nothing has been run or tested.
